question: Sporangia blobs contain cells or spores that can eventually develop into new Rhizopus individuals. Such asexual reproduction is known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**spore formation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Spore formation is a type of asexual reproduction where an organism forms spores that can develop into new individuals.
 
• In Rhizopus, sporangia are structures that produce and release spores.
 
• These spores are typically resistant to harsh environmental conditions, aiding in the survival of the organism.
 
• When conditions are favorable, spores germinate and grow into new Rhizopus individuals.
 
• Spore formation is common in fungi, algae, and some non-flowering plants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rhizopus**

 
 
• Rhizopus is a genus of common fungi, often found on bread, fruits, and vegetables.
 
• It is known for its fast-growing nature and is used in industrial applications like the production of biochemicals.
 
 
 
• **Spore**
 
 
• A spore is a reproductive cell capable of developing into a new individual without fusion with another cell.
 
• In fungi, spores are usually produced in large numbers to increase the chances of survival.
 
 
 
• **Asexual Reproduction**
 
 
• Asexual reproduction is a mode of reproduction where offspring are produced by a single parent without the involvement of gamete fusion.
 
• It results in genetically identical individuals, known as clones.
 
 
 
• **Favorable Conditions for Germination**
 
 
• Favorable conditions typically include adequate moisture, suitable temperature, and the presence of nutrients.
 
• These conditions trigger the germination process, leading to the growth of new organisms.
